The Western Christian writes about the persecution of the saints. The endurance the text demands. The mark no true believer will take. The beast system rising to devour the faithful.

The “we” in the piece is American. The frame is suburban. The saints being persecuted are people who might one day lose their social media accounts or get uninvited from a church that went seeker-friendly.

This is not theology. It is a genre.

And the genre has a name.

Main Character Syndrome: the assumption that one’s own context is the primary stage on which the text is fulfilled.

The Numbers Are Already a Verdict

In 1900, Africa had approximately 10 million Christians.

Today that number exceeds 700 million.

By 2050, projections place African Christianity above 1.3 billion, the single largest Christian population on earth, concentrated on a single continent.

In the same window, Western Christianity has been hollowing out. European cathedrals are tourist destinations. American church attendance has been in decline for four consecutive decades. The branch that produces the most eschatology, the most commentary, the most end-times podcasts and prophecy conferences and beast-system theory, that branch is thinning. Its young are leaving. Its buildings are emptying. Its cultural influence is receding at a rate its own data cannot explain away.

The branch that is dying is convinced it is the vine.

Jesus already gave us the diagnostic tool for this situation. He did not leave it ambiguous.

You will know them by their fruit.

Not by their conferences. Not by their commentary volumes. Not by their eschatological charts or their seminary credentials or their publishing output. By their fruit. The tree that is producing — seed, growth, yield, root systems going down into difficult soil — that tree does not need to argue for its vitality. The argument is already in the ground.

The tree that spends its energy theorizing about the fruit it will one day produce, while its own canopy thins decade by decade, that tree has a fruit problem. And Jesus was not gentle about what you do with trees that don’t produce.

The Witness They Are Standing On

The church that has already lived under the extraction system is not hypothetical.

The Congolese believer did not theorize about what it would feel like when a beast system installed a “transitional government” after a manufactured crisis. They watched it happen to their country. Repeatedly. Create the problem, arrive as the savior, install the new order, that is not an American theory about what might be coming. That is the lived testimony of the African church across the entire post-colonial period.

The Ethiopian Orthodox community preserved the 81-book canon through Italian occupation. Through the Derg’s Marxist suppression. Through sustained institutional pressure to conform to Western theological norms and Western canon decisions. They did not read about endurance in a prophecy book. They practiced it across sixteen centuries of unbroken witness.

The underground Chinese church did not speculate about what persecution would cost. They counted the cost and kept meeting.

The Nigerian believer living on the fault line between Christian south and pressure from the north does not need a conference to explain what it means to endure to the end.

These are not supporting characters in someone else’s story. They are the primary witnesses to everything Revelation says about faithful endurance under beast-system pressure. And the Western eschatology conversation treats them as the establishing shot, the backdrop that proves the main story before the camera returns to the real saints, the ones writing the commentary.

Revelation says the beast has authority over every tribe, tongue, people, and nation. The Western reader hears “every nation” and treats it as a wide-angle lens that quickly zooms back to them.

Laodicea Is a Mailing Address.

The seven letters in Revelation go to seven specific churches. Six of them receive either commendation, rebuke, or both. One of them receives the sharpest rebuke in the sequence.

The lukewarm church. Not cold, not hot. Comfortable. Self-sufficient. Rich. Convinced it lacks nothing. Told by the text directly:

You are wretched, pitiful, poor, blind, and naked.

The letter does not go to the persecuted church. Persecution has a clarifying effect on temperature. The Smyrna church is being crushed and the text calls it rich. The letter to the lukewarm church goes to the comfortable one, the one whose wealth has insulated it from the friction that produces heat, whose ease has produced the spiritual equivalent of a body that has forgotten it has nerve endings.

Laodicea is not a first-century cautionary tale that Western Christianity reads about with detached interest. It is a diagnostic category. And the church whose canopy has been thinning for forty years, while producing more eschatology than any other tradition in history, while the genuinely persecuted church grows at a rate with no modern parallel, that church should sit with the Laodicea letter longer than it sits with its beast-system theories.

The mark of the beast the comfortable church needs to worry about first is not a chip. The character of Babylon absorbed so gradually that the temperature never triggers alarm. You are not conquered suddenly. You drift. And then one morning you write about persecution using “we” and mean people who look like you, live where you live, and have never once had their ability to buy and sell threatened by anything except their own credit score.

What the Fruit Says

The 700 million is not a statistic. It is testimony.

The church that carries the most complete surviving canon is African. The church with the oldest continuous liturgical practice is African. The church that has endured occupation, suppression, and sustained institutional pressure without losing its canonical witness is African. The church that is growing fastest in the soil closest to where the text was written is African and Middle Eastern and Asian.

This is not a numbers argument. Growth alone proves nothing, every extraction system grows until it collapses. The witness here is the combination: growth, canonical preservation, and endurance under actual extraction pressure. All three, together, in the same body. That is what fruit looks like. That is what Jesus was pointing at.

The church that is thinning, while producing the most theory about what it will endure in the days ahead, is Western.

Jesus said you will know them by their fruit. He did not add an exemption for doctrinal volume. He did not say the tree with the best eschatological system gets extra credit while the canopy thins. He said fruit. Visible, countable, rooted-in-the-ground fruit.

The fruit map and the commentary map do not overlap. That is not an accident. That is the answer to a question the Western church is not yet asking.

The West is not the main character in this story.

It is the warning.
